Markets.title: Big US bank stocks head for longest weekly losing streak since 2008
Markets.summary: Major US bank stocks are experiencing their longest weekly losing streak since the 2008 financial crisis. This downturn is driven by mixed quarterly earnings, rising inflation, and concerns that artificial intelligence will disrupt financial services.

Markets.title: Chip selloff deepens Wall Street losses as doubts grew over AI returns
Markets.summary: Semiconductor stocks dropped amid growing doubts about the profitability of artificial intelligence investments, dragging down major US indexes. The Nasdaq 100 fell 1.8%, marking its longest losing streak since 2008.

Markets.title: Crompton Greaves Consumer Electricals Ltd Q2 Results: Profit surges 65% to Rs 124 crore
Markets.summary: Crompton Greaves Consumer Electricals reported a 65 percent increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 124 crore for the September quarter. Revenue from operations jumped 18.15 percent, driven by strong growth in the electric consumer durable segment, particularly fans and appliances.

Markets.title: Cult.fit receives Sebi approval for proposed IPO
Markets.summary: Fitness chain Cult.fit has received regulatory approval from Sebi for an initial public offering that includes a fresh issue of up to Rs 950 crore and an offer for sale. The company's expansion of nationwide fitness operations drove a 36.26% revenue increase and a significant improvement in its adjusted EBITDA margin in FY26.

Markets.title: US stocks: S&P 500 muted as AI concerns hit chip stocks; bank gains lift Dow
Markets.summary: The S&P 500 remained flat as losses in semiconductor and AI-related stocks were offset by gains in major banks like Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase. Market sentiment was further influenced by rising debt concerns among AI companies and new inflation data.
